data.narrative:
Quantum Source is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised approximately $77 million to date. The quantum computing sector comprises a modest but active peer universe of 11 companies—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private entities including Quantinuum, IonQ (pre-IPO phase), and Infleqtion.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable in this instance. Despite identifying 5 same-sector peers, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), leaving zero datapoints that meet the minimum threshold of three comparables. A broadened all-sector median would introduce unacceptable methodological noise given the technical and capital-intensity divergence across quantum computing platforms and architectures. The extreme heterogeneity of the peer set—spanning quantum annealing, gate-based, and ion-trap approaches—further undermines direct multiples-based triangulation without stage-specific granularity.

Given these constraints, a robust valuation range cannot be derived from the provided dataset. Additional inputs are required: (1) revenue or ARR figures for Quantum Source and peer companies; (2) stage-matched private financings or secondary transactions within the quantum computing sector; or (3) explicit cost-of-capital assumptions enabling discounted cash flow analysis. The sparsity of late-stage or public quantum computing comparables at Series A entry pricing limits confidence in any single method. Future analysis should prioritize expansion of private Series A or B transaction data in this sector.
